questions.q: How does signature-based detection decide that traffic is malicious?
options: It only looks at traffic volume, never payload content
It matches traffic against a database of known attack patterns or exploit fingerprints
It requires a human to manually approve every packet
It randomly samples a percentage of all traffic
questions.explain: Signature-based detection compares traffic against documented attack patterns, the same basic idea as antivirus matching known malware.

questions.q: What is the main weakness of signature-based detection?
options: It's blind to novel attacks that don't yet have a documented signature
It requires more computing power than anomaly-based detection
It only works on encrypted traffic
It can never detect any attack, known or unknown
questions.explain: Signature-based detection is only as good as its signature database, so a brand-new technique with no signature goes undetected.

questions.q: How does anomaly-based detection decide that something is suspicious?
options: It can only be used on host-based systems, never network traffic
It ignores all network traffic and only reads log files
It matches traffic against a fixed list of known attack signatures
It builds a baseline of normal behavior and flags meaningful deviations from it
questions.explain: Anomaly-based detection learns what normal looks like and flags traffic that deviates from that baseline.

questions.q: Why does anomaly-based detection tend to generate more false positives than signature-based detection?
options: It only runs once a day
Legitimately unusual but harmless behavior can still deviate from the learned baseline
False positives are actually impossible with anomaly-based detection
It has no database of any kind to reference
questions.explain: The anomaly engine can't distinguish unusual-but-harmless behavior from unusual-and-malicious behavior, so both trip the same alarm.

questions.q: Why do most modern detection platforms run both signature-based and anomaly-based engines together?
options: There is no benefit to combining them, but vendors do it anyway
Signature-based detection has been fully replaced by anomaly-based detection in all modern tools
Signatures give fast, precise coverage for known threats while anomaly detection covers novel ones, balancing precision and coverage
Running both is required by federal regulation
questions.explain: The hybrid approach gets the speed and precision of signatures plus the broader, novel-attack coverage of anomaly detection.
